title: Best Dehumidifier for Basement Mold & Musty Smells (2026)
h1: The Best Basement Dehumidifiers for Mold, Damp and Musty Smells
dek: Below-grade air is cool, still and damp — exactly what mold wants. These dehumidifiers drain themselves and keep the basement in the safe zone.
description: The best dehumidifiers for basement mold and musty smells, with self-draining pump picks, low-temperature models and the right size and setting for your space.
intro: If you're shopping for a **dehumidifier for basement mold**, you're fighting the hardest room in the house. Basements sit below grade, breathe moisture through concrete, rarely get fresh air and often stay cool — a combination mold loves. The EPA warns that mold can get started on a damp surface within **24 to 48 hours**, which is why a basement dehumidifier has to run reliably and get rid of its water without you.

That changes what matters. Drainage comes first: a pump or a gravity hose beats a bucket you have to haul upstairs. Cold tolerance comes next, because a standard unit can frost over in a chilly basement. Then capacity, measured under today's DOE test, and a humidistat that holds a real number. We weighed all five of the picks below on those points, using published ratings, manuals, recall records and owner reports.
topPicksLead: For most basements, the **Midea Cube 50-Pint** is the one to buy: full 50-pint capacity, an unusually large tank and an easy hose connection for hands-free draining.

Smaller 20- and 35-pint Cubes use the same design if your space is modest.

blocks.text: One more figure worth knowing: building-science guidance holds that a large share of the air on your first floor rises from the basement or crawl space. Drying the basement is often the real fix for a musty smell upstairs.

We don't lab-test. We compare capacity under the 2019 DOE test procedure, ENERGY STAR listings, manufacturer manuals (for drainage options, pump lift and minimum operating temperature) and the CPSC recall database. Then we read owner reviews for patterns: pumps that fail early, sensors that read far off, units that ice up in cool basements.

For basements we weighted drainage highest, followed by low-temperature performance, real DOE capacity and humidistat precision. As of our last check, none of the current-generation models here are affected by a CPSC recall; the remaining recalls in this category involve older pre-2019 units.

sections.heading: What to look for in a basement dehumidifier

items.label: A drainage plan
items.text: Floor drain below the unit? A gravity hose is free and reliable. No drain? Get a built-in pump so water goes up to a sink or out a window.

items.label: Enough real capacity
items.text: Size by the DOE 2019 rating. Today's 50-pint unit removes roughly what an old 70-pint model claimed.

items.label: Cold-weather tolerance
items.text: Below about 65°F, insist on auto-defrost. In a basement that sits near 40°F, step up to a commercial unit. If yours is already icing, read [dehumidifier freezing up](/guides/dehumidifier-freezing-up/).

items.label: A real humidistat
items.text: You want to dial in a percentage so the unit cycles off at your target instead of running non-stop.

items.label: Smart placement
items.text: Keep it a foot or more from walls and away from the dryer. Central placement dries the whole space more evenly.

blocks.text: Smaller basements may only need a mid-size unit — our 1,000 sq ft picks cover those. For a deeper walkthrough, see the [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/).

sections.heading: What should a dehumidifier be set on in a basement?

blocks.text: Set the humidistat to **45–50%** and let the unit cycle. That keeps you comfortably below the 60% threshold where mold and dust mites thrive, without wasting electricity chasing a bone-dry reading. In a cold basement, 50% is plenty; pushing lower mostly adds run time and icing risk.

blocks.title: Check the number independently
blocks.text: Built-in sensors can drift several points. A cheap standalone hygrometer at the far end of the basement tells you whether the whole space is dry, not just the air right next to the unit.

sections.heading: Will a dehumidifier get rid of basement mold and smell?

blocks.text: A dehumidifier stops mold from growing and fades that musty smell by removing the moisture both depend on. It won't kill or remove mold that's already there. Clean visible growth first, fix any water entry (gutters, grading, cracks), then run the dehumidifier to keep the space below 50%. For more detail, see [does a dehumidifier help with mold?](/guides/does-a-dehumidifier-help-with-mold/).

If a portable can't keep up, or you'd rather not see a unit at all, a ducted **basement dehumidification system** — a whole-house unit installed in the mechanical room — is the permanent answer. Our [whole-house dehumidifier guide](/best/best-whole-house-dehumidifier/) compares the main options.

The **Midea Cube 50-Pint** is the best basement dehumidifier for most homes, pairing full capacity with a tank you rarely need to empty. Choose the **hOmeLabs HME1003** when there's no floor drain and you need a pump, save with the **Frigidaire FHDD5034Y1**, and go commercial with the **AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S** for a cold, unfinished basement you want dry for good. Set any of them to 45–50%, and the musty smell should fade within a couple of weeks.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier for basement mold?
faqs.a: For most basements, the Midea Cube 50-Pint, thanks to its full DOE capacity and large tank. If there's no floor drain, choose a pump model like the hOmeLabs HME1003 so it can run continuously and keep humidity below the level mold needs.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier with a pump for a basement?
faqs.a: The hOmeLabs HME1003 is our top pump pick for large or wet basements. The Ivation IVADH50PWP2 is another ENERGY STAR pump option, and the AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S is the commercial choice for cold basements.

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier do I need for a basement?
faqs.a: Most basements need a 35- to 50-pint unit under the DOE 2019 rating. Choose 50 pints for a large, very damp or previously flooded basement, and 35 pints for a smaller or mildly damp one.

faqs.q: What humidity should a basement dehumidifier be set to?
faqs.a: Around 45–50%. That keeps the space safely below 60%, where mold thrives, without running the unit more than necessary.

faqs.q: Will a dehumidifier work in a cold basement?
faqs.a: Only if it's designed for it. Below about 65°F, standard units can frost over, so look for auto-defrost. Commercial units like the AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S keep working down to about 36°F.

faqs.q: Will a dehumidifier get rid of a musty basement smell?
faqs.a: Usually, yes, once humidity stays below 50% for a few weeks. If the smell persists, look for hidden mold or a water leak; our [musty smell picks](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-musty-smell/) cover tougher cases.
